title: Identification, Design, and Application of Noncoding Cis-Regulatory Elements.
one_liner_zh: 综述顺式调控元件(CRE)的鉴定、设计与应用，涵盖与转录因子等反式因子的互作及深度学习预测设计，但未聚焦TF-DNA三维结合机制与建模，方法可迁移至本课题。
abstract: Cis-regulatory elements (CREs) play a pivotal role in orchestrating interactions with trans-regulatory factors such as transcription factors, RNA-binding proteins, and noncoding RNAs. These interactions are fundamental to the molecular architecture underpinning complex and diverse biological functions in living organisms, facilitating a myriad of sophisticated and dynamic processes. The rapid advancement in the identification and characterization of these regulatory elements has been marked by initiatives such as the Encyclopedia of DNA Elements (ENCODE) project, which represents a significant milestone in the field. Concurrently, the development of CRE detection technologies, exemplified by massively parallel reporter assays, has progressed at an impressive pace, providing powerful tools for CRE discovery. The exponential growth of multimodal functional genomic data has necessitated the application of advanced analytical methods. Deep learning algorithms, particularly large language models, have emerged as invaluable tools for deconstructing the intricate nucleotide sequences governing CRE function. These advancements facilitate precise predictions of CRE activity and enable the de novo design of CREs. A deeper understanding of CRE operational dynamics is crucial for harnessing their versatile regulatory properties. Such insights are instrumental in refining gene therapy techniques, enhancing the efficacy of selective breeding programs, pushing the boundaries of genetic innovation, and opening new possibilities in microbial synthetic biology.
abstract_zh: 顺式调控元件（cis-regulatory elements, CREs）在协调与反式调控因子（如转录因子、RNA结合蛋白和非编码RNA）的相互作用中发挥着关键作用。这些相互作用是支撑生物体内复杂多样生物学功能的分子架构基础，促进了众多精密且动态的过程。这些调控元件的识别与表征进展迅速，以DNA元件百科全书（ENCODE）项目等举措为标志，该项目代表了该领域的一个重要里程碑。同时，CRE检测技术的发展，例如大规模平行报告基因分析，其进展速度令人瞩目，为CRE发现提供了强大工具。多模态功能基因组数据的指数级增长，促使先进分析方法的应用成为必要。深度学习算法，尤其是大型语言模型，已成为解析调控CRE功能的复杂核苷酸序列的宝贵工具。这些进展促进了CRE活性的精确预测，并实现了CRE的从头设计。深入理解CRE运作动态对于利用其多功能调控特性至关重要。此类见解有助于精炼基因治疗技术、提升选择性育种项目的效率、推动遗传创新的边界，并在微生物合成生物学领域开辟新可能性。
